races.name: Tramore Directors Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Louiescall
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with Good-ground form (2nd over 2m at Leopardstown on Good); Daniel King booking for David Harry Kelly confirms intent to lead, and 18 days between runs leaves him fresh — the key question is whether his hurdle jumping is accurate enough to sustain an uncontested lead throughout.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's six-year-old has placed four times at this level and wears a tongue-strap; a natural hold-up horse who will be further forward than ideal given field composition, which dilutes his chance — his best form (four seconds) has come when able to finish off races from behind.

runners_data.name: Speed For Fun
runners_data.note: Mullins and Brian Hayes is always a formidable combination, and this horse's only hurdle run produced a second on Good ground; limited recent form (one run, fell) means the fitness question is real, though the class angle cannot be dismissed entirely.

runners_data.name: Ballybollen
runners_data.note: De Bromhead and Darragh O'Keeffe send out a prominent-style five-year-old with one start showing a fourth on Good ground — sits naturally just behind the leader and is ideally positioned if Louiescall weakens; light weight at 158lbs is a marginal advantage.

runners_data.name: Cairo King
runners_data.note: 829 days off the track is the dominant factor here; previously wore a tongue-tie, has shown a tendency to fade in finishes, and even his best effort (third) came on Soft ground — this comeback run is a significant unknown and the amateur rider (Josh Younge, 7lb claimer) adds further risk.

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the mount on a horse that prefers to race from the rear; headgear includes hood and tongue-tie in the past, and while he placed twice in 2024, his natural hold-up style will be squeezed in a field stacked with closers — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 reflects genuine positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Grabat
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton's five-year-old has two runs over hurdles, the best a sixth on Good ground over 2m; Niall Moore (5lb claimer) takes the ride and this horse has shown nothing yet to suggest it can challenge off OR 120.

runners_data.name: Sankofa
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly runs a second horse alongside Louiescall; form reads 3-9 and a fading tendency has been flagged — 13 days since last run is sharp, but the nine-length defeat last time and the finishing concern make this a tough ask at this level.

runners_data.name: Bobby Kirova
runners_data.note: Michael Butler's four-year-old showed a third on Good ground over 1m6f and brings Flat speed into the equation; a natural hold-up runner placed in midfield by necessity, and Paddy Cody's 7lb claim helps, but STYLE_FIT 0.91 signals it won't get the ground-saving position it needs.

runners_data.name: Ivatt
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old has been running on the Flat (placed at Dundalk on Standard) and makes an interesting switch to hurdles; T14 of 4/42 shows Elliott in reasonable form, Danny Gilligan takes the ride, and the horse's prominent style suits this race shape — the x-factor of a Flat recruit making hurdling debut is worth noting.

races.paceDynamic: Louiescall is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at a pace entirely of Daniel King's choosing — this is a textbook uncontested lead scenario over 2m½f on Good ground at Tramore. The remaining field is dominated by hold-up types, with Penzance, Bobby Kirova, and Captain Hanley all natural rear-runners who have been mapped to midfield simply because the field cannot accommodate every hold-up horse at the back. Ballybollen and Ivatt are the only genuine prominent horses who might push forward and give Louiescall some company in the early stages, but neither is likely to force a genuinely searching gallop. This race shape heavily favours Louiescall to control tempo and a horse with class, jumping ability, or a prominent pitch to challenge in the straight — hold-up horses racing out of role from a compressed midfield will be disadvantaged. More front-running and prominent types exist in this field than the rear of the map shows; Louiescall will secure the lead comfortably, with Ballybollen and Ivatt the likeliest to sit closest behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Louiescall Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Louiescall leads at a fair but uncontested gallop and sets a rhythm that suits his jumping.
scenarios.body: Louiescall bowls along in front, jumping accurately under Daniel King, and the hold-up horses in a compressed midfield never get the sustained gallop they need to close the gap in the straight; Ballybollen and Ivatt, tracking prominently, are best placed to challenge but Louiescall's control of tempo makes him very hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Reels Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Louiescall's jumping is flawed or he sets a pace too strong for his stamina reserves.
scenarios.body: Louiescall idles or makes a jumping error in the back straight, handing a prominent challenger the initiative; Ballybollen (De Bromhead, Darragh O'Keeffe) or Ivatt (Elliott, 4yo) are ideally positioned to pick up the pieces without having burned their petrol chasing the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Louiescall cuts out a strong pace that depletes the prominent horses and leaves the race truly up for grabs in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A sustained gallop forces the prominent runners into trouble in the straight, and a hold-up horse racing closer than their natural role — Speed For Fun (Mullins, Hayes, Good-form figures) — is able to pick off tired rivals; the redistribution of true hold-up horses to midfield means this scenario is mildly more plausible than a genuine closing run from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race is messy, involving jumping errors from the principals, and the form book is thrown out.
scenarios.body: Cairo King (829 days off, returning from a long break) or Grabat benefit from a chaotic race in which more fancied runners are eliminated or checked; these horses are at very long odds and this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong for others.

watchPoints.text: Louiescall's jumping technique is the single most important variable — any mistake at a hurdle under Daniel King in the back straight could immediately hand Ballybollen or Ivatt a decisive advantage that proves impossible to recover.

Ivatt's debut over hurdles for Gordon Elliott is a significant unknown; Elliott juveniles switching from Flat to jumping can be dramatically better or worse than their Flat form suggests, and Danny Gilligan's ride could go either way.

Cairo King has not run for 829 days and lines up with a 7lb claiming amateur — monitor in the parade ring for any signs of the horse being trained purely for fitness, as interference or a jumping blunder from a rusty rival could disrupt the pack behind Louiescall.

Penzance, Bobby Kirova, and Captain Hanley are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield — if they all make forward moves simultaneously approaching the final flight, a traffic and interference situation in the straight is plausible and could unsettle each other's runs.

Speed For Fun's Mullins/Hayes combination routinely improves markedly from a first run back; the horse's single hurdle placing on Good ground is the most relevant piece of form if it has been given a preparatory run last time out.

races.name: Frank Gillane Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Returned just nine days ago with a win over 16f on Good, bringing strong same-going credentials (1W2P from 10 similar runs); a natural hold-up horse who will need to find daylight in a busy rear group, but in-form and well-weighted at OR 96.

runners_data.name: Annie's Angel
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a hold-up profile and no wins or places on Good ground across five attempts in similar conditions; the Kenneally 5lb claim helps slightly but the form string and going record make it hard to get excited.

runners_data.name: Doctor Confusion
runners_data.note: The only front-runner in the race, able to bowl along unchallenged for Henry De Bromhead under Darragh O'Keeffe; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is relevant here in the sense that it is technically a prominent runner in a field that suits it — its chance is real precisely because no one will pressure it.

runners_data.name: Ina Mina
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 17f trip on Good 13 days ago for Terence O'Brien, and John Shinnick keeps the partnership intact; hold-up in style but Tramore's shape can bring those horses into play from the home turn, and the recent course-and-distance win is the standout form line.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine, holds solid Good-ground form (1W3P from 14 similar runs) but the recent string shows P-0-6-5-5 and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim has limits against in-form rivals; hold-up style means traffic will be a factor in a 16-runner field.

runners_data.name: Colesberg
runners_data.note: Not seen in 93 days and has only one run on similar going from four attempts; the long absence and limited Good-ground exposure are two reasons to treat this lightly despite being lightly weighted at OR 93.

runners_data.name: Glendower
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse whose true style places it further back than the midfield position shown here — its best form (3 places from 11 on Good) has come when able to race at its own pace, and being squeezed forward against its nature reduces its winning prospects.

runners_data.name: Truckers Cruising
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's charge has been placed in midfield on the map due to the overcrowded rear, but its record clearly shows a horse that wants to come from well off the pace; four of its last five runs on Good produced finishes of 5th or worse, and there is no compelling reason to think it navigates a busy field.

runners_data.name: Lanzhou
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago — that rapid turnaround is the headline concern — and the finishing tendency to fade late is a further worry in a strongly-run 2m½f; though a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield by necessity, its recent form (0-0-9-1-0-7) on Good gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Owl's Delight
runners_data.note: A prominent racer at OR 84 who fades in the finish, making it a likely pace companion to Doctor Confusion in the early stages but an unlikely winner; has finished 6th or worse in all five recent Good-ground starts, and the fade flag is a meaningful deduction.

runners_data.name: Vairue
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who has shown one win and a place from 15 Good-ground starts; naturally races from hold-up positions but has been mapped to midfield given the overcrowded rear — at OR 83 and with a fall last time in the form string, this looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, the freshest turnaround in the field, which is the dominant factor regardless of style; hold-up by nature and placed in midfield only because the rear is full — five recent Good-ground runs have produced no win or place, and the fitness question from a 48-hour gap cannot be overlooked.

runners_data.name: Depeche Mo
runners_data.note: Off the track for 445 days — the longest absence in the field — and returns at OR 74 with a prominent style; two places from 11 Good-ground runs suggest some ability in similar conditions, but a 15-month layoff makes this a significant risk.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Has a win and three places from 14 Good-ground starts, giving it one of the stronger same-going CVs in the lower handicap ranks; naturally hold-up but mapped to midfield, and at OR 73 the weight advantage could count if given a clear passage in the home straight.

runners_data.name: Doyen Og
runners_data.note: Consistently fades in the finish and has not won in 13 attempts on Good — both those facts weigh heavily; its redistribution to midfield reflects the overcrowded hold-up group rather than any change in running style, and OR 72 tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Maxios Lady
runners_data.note: Off the track for 324 days and returns with a fade tendency and a record of 0W0P from four Good-ground runs; at OR 72, the absence and the form make this one of the harder horses to assess positively, regardless of how the race is run.

races.paceDynamic: Doctor Confusion is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse field and, crucially, faces no genuine pressure from another pace-setter, meaning Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Tramore. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up and midfield types — Truckers Cruising, Glendower, Lanzhou, Vairue, Cinnabar Moth, Surviving Murmansk and others are all natural hold-up horses who have been redistributed forward on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded, not because they will genuinely race there. Owl's Delight and Depeche Mo offer some prominent coverage but neither is likely to seriously challenge Doctor Confusion for the lead, leaving the pace controlled and measured throughout. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel efficiently in midfield or prominent positions and produce a sustained gallop from the home turn rather than a sharp late burst — genuine closers will face a wall of traffic and a pace insufficient to string the field out, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Front Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Doctor Confusion dictates a comfortable tempo unchallenged and the hold-up horses cannot navigate traffic in time.
scenarios.body: Doctor Confusion bowls along at a fair clip on Good ground, the crowded midfield creates interference for the late runners, and those tracking in touch from prominent positions inherit the spoils as closers are baulked.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Trackers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and one or two horses travelling smoothly just off the pace produce a clean run through.
scenarios.body: The moderate but honest gallop set by Doctor Confusion rewards horses who sit two or three lengths off in a handy spot, with Ina Mina and Liberated Light both boasting good-ground form and the scope to pick up from the home turn at Tramore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Weave Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and the field concertinas, creating a scramble that allows a well-held horse to pick through late.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish would theoretically suit Pahlavi or Surviving Murmansk, both of whom have shown ability to stay on when given a clear passage, but the overcrowded hold-up group makes a clean run far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Doctor Confusion, given a soft lead, finds extra reserves when asked and none of the prominent horses can sustain their challenge over the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: A front-runner left alone at a manageable tempo can occasionally outfox a field that is poorly positioned, and at Tramore's sharp track the home bend can catch hold-up horses flat-footed if the leader has already kicked.

watchPoints.text: Doctor Confusion holds a potentially race-defining advantage as the sole front-runner — if Darragh O'Keeffe is allowed to coast in front unchallenged, the steady pace could be enough to see off a congested hold-up field at Tramore.

Lanzhou ran just three days ago and Cinnabar Moth just two days ago — both are hold-up types already fighting for space at the rear, and the rapid turnarounds could produce unpredictable early behaviour in a 16-runner field, creating traffic risks for those around them.

The hold-up group is severely overcrowded: Truckers Cruising, Glendower, Vairue, Surviving Murmansk, Doyen Og and Maxios Lady are all natural closers competing for the same ground — watch for a bunching incident on the home turn that could eliminate multiple contenders at once.

Ina Mina's recent Good-ground win over the same trip gives it the standout form line in terms of conditions; watch whether John Shinnick can find a position just off Doctor Confusion's pace rather than being swamped in the hold-up group.

Depeche Mo returns from 445 days off — monitor its early behaviour in the parade ring and at the start, as a prominent-style runner returning from a long absence in a fast-filling field can unsettle those around it before a yard has been run.

races.name: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Something Fabulous
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on good for McConnell, placed at 19f on good — the stamina profile fits this 2m5½f trip well; 134 days off is worth monitoring but the trainer has a strong recent strike rate, and a prominent pitch should be attainable given the natural lead battle ahead.

runners_data.name: Ajp Falco
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has repeatedly failed to see out his races (five runs, no win or place), and the fade-in-finish flag is a serious concern at this stamina trip; head gear worn, and a trainer in poor recent form (0/11 over 14 days) does little to strengthen the case.

runners_data.name: Goodmancon
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile suits this pace scenario and he has placed on good going twice in five similar-going starts; racing 12 days after his last run for a trainer with minimal recent activity, but his third last time on soft-ish ground suggests he is in decent nick.

runners_data.name: L'As de Watt
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a placed effort at 16f on good, but has been beaten a long way back in recent starts including an eighth over the same 18f trip; the 5lb claimer Niall Moore takes a small bite off the top, yet the overall form trajectory is flat.

runners_data.name: Market Ready
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed at 16f on soft and second at 16f on soft — the step up to 2m5½f on good is a stamina question not yet answered; Anna McGuinness's 7lb claim helps, and three placed efforts in five runs suggest consistency without brilliance.

runners_data.name: South Of Killerig
runners_data.note: Strong on the P route but has not won and the recent form includes a string of pull-ups and poor finishes; this is a genuine hold-up horse that the pace map has pushed into midfield because there are more hold-up types than rear slots — racing out of its natural position tempers its chance, and a STYLE_FIT penalty of 0.90 applies.

runners_data.name: Bury Your Past
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with only one run in the book (eighth over 18f on good) and a fade-in-finish flag — almost nothing to go on, and Conor Smithers's 7lb claim is the headline angle; the trip is unexplored territory for a horse with this thin a profile.

runners_data.name: Eyecanboogie
runners_data.note: Has placed at 16f on good but has also fallen and unseated recently, suggesting jumping reliability is a concern over 2m5½f; McNamara has sent out one winner in the last 10 days, and the form string includes a worrying U which must be factored in.

runners_data.name: Flowing Fast
runners_data.note: Another O'Loughlin-trained runner alongside Bury Your Past with minimal form — one run, eleventh over 17f on good, plus a fade-in-finish flag; nothing in the record to suggest it can handle a genuinely run 2m5½f maiden hurdle, and the P-FP80 recent form is alarming.

runners_data.name: Lady Lena
runners_data.note: Mullins and Hayes is the strongest trainer-jockey combination in the race, and both her starts have yielded places (second and third); absent 294 days — the freshness is a genuine unknown at this trip, but she is the most likely horse to control the front and the class of her connections separates her from most rivals.

runners_data.name: Thelittleredfox
runners_data.note: Has a single run (twelfth over 17f on good) and a fade-in-finish warning — no meaningful form to assess in a maiden hurdle over this stamina trip; the Denis Ahern yard is quiet (0/1 over 14 days) and this horse is essentially unexposed in the most cautionary sense.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Lena (Mullins/Hayes) and Ajp Falco (Kelly/Flanagan) are both confirmed front-runners in an 11-runner field over 2m5½f on good ground at Tramore, meaning the early gallop will be genuinely contested rather than dawdled. With two horses committed to leading, the pace is unlikely to be manufactured or false — expect an honest, even tempo from the outset that tests stamina into the final climb. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with proven staying power at this trip and going, as the contested lead should stretch the field out and prevent a bunched sprint finish. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Lady Lena, with the Mullins/Hayes alliance and fresher legs (294 days since last run adding unknown), is most likely to control the rail position ahead of Ajp Falco, with Something Fabulous the most likely to secure a genuine prominent pitch — runners pushed back from their natural berths should be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Lena and Ajp Falco set an even, sustained gallop that stretches the field from halfway and the race is won by a horse who travels prominently and stays every yard.
scenarios.body: Lady Lena controls matters from the front with Hayes dictating, but the pressure of Ajp Falco ensures the pace is genuine enough to expose any stamina limitations; Something Fabulous, who has won over 16f on good and placed at 19f, is ideally positioned to pick off a tiring leader in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two confirmed front-runners — most likely Lady Lena — dominates the lead, repels Ajp Falco early, and simply gallops the others into submission over the 2m5½f trip.
scenarios.body: Lady Lena, trained by Mullins and ridden by Hayes, has placed in both starts and has never been asked this far before, but a dominant hold on the lead at a true gallop over this stamina-testing trip could see her grind relentlessly to the line; Ajp Falco's tendency to fade in the finish makes it unlikely to sustain the challenge, leaving Lady Lena clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested front-running duel between Lady Lena and Ajp Falco burns both out, leaving the field vulnerable to a fresh closer producing a sustained late run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Goodmancon and Eyecanboogie are the most plausible beneficiaries given genuine hold-up profiles, but the redistribution of South Of Killerig — a true hold-up horse operating out of its natural position — limits the depth of late closers available; Goodmancon's recent third on similar going and Eyecanboogie's placed effort over 16f on good ground give them each a residual shout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If neither Lady Lena nor Ajp Falco settles into a true rhythm and the race becomes stop-start, creating a bunched finish that plays into the hands of lightly raced or unexposed types.
scenarios.body: Bury Your Past, Flowing Fast and Thelittleredfox are all unknowns whose lightly raced profiles leave them with untapped improvement, and a truly chaotic race could mask their raw inexperience; however, all three carry fade-in-finish flags and uncertain form, making this the least reliable scenario to construct a case around.

watchPoints.text: Lady Lena (Mullins/Hayes) has been off 294 days — watch the market closely pre-race; if she is heavily supported despite the long absence, connections clearly believe the freshness is no barrier to a forward run.

Ajp Falco's tendency to fade in the finish combined with front-running duties over 2m5½f creates a genuine risk of stopping badly in the straight — watch whether Sean Flanagan attempts to restrain and track rather than lead, which would alter the entire pace picture.

South Of Killerig is a true hold-up horse that the field's pace imbalance has pushed into a midfield position — if it cannot settle back into its natural role from a midfield berth, it may use energy early and fail to produce its best late run.

The O'Loughlin yard runs Bury Your Past and Flowing Fast in the same race — watch for any drifting or market confidence that separates the two, as connections will know which is the more forward of the pair.

Goodmancon races just 12 days after his last start — watch his pre-race demeanour and whether Ian Power attempts to switch him off early, as a horse running this frequently can either be in peak form or carrying residual fatigue.

races.name: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Carry On Heidi
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed in three of her last five starts; Jerry Baragry sends her here after 157 days off, which is a notable layoff, but her good-going figures (4 runs, 1 win, 2 placed) are solid and she shapes as a natural fit for a race run at an honest pace.

runners_data.name: Costanuci
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a poor strike rate despite 15 runs on good ground (0 wins, 5 placed); John Queally has placed 3 runners from 3 in the last 14 days which is a minor positive, but Costanuci's recent form string of 5-P-8-5-2 shows she finds the frame rarely and offers limited upside against better-credentialed rivals.

runners_data.name: Ellens Pride
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with headgear (p) who has finished no better than fourth in her last seven runs on good ground; Daniel King takes the ride but there is nothing in the historical pattern to suggest she can mount a sustained challenge in a race likely to be run at pace, and her jumping may be tested in a beginners' chase.

runners_data.name: Future Prospect
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Willie Mullins ridden by Danny Mullins; two wins and six places from 11 good-ground starts underline her competence on this surface, and headgear (h) suggests she is managed for concentration — she holds a strong each-way claims if she handles the fencing at this trip.

runners_data.name: Kaylasjet
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with an alarming recent form string of P-P-4-P-6; only one run on good ground in the data and a 7lb claimer in the saddle limits confidence, while her jumping reliability in a beginners' chase over 2m6f is a significant question mark.

runners_data.name: La Note Verte
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from the Mullins yard ridden by J J Slevin, winner of 3 from 8 good-ground starts with solid placed record; she has been running consistently at shorter trips (16f) so the step to 2m6f is a genuine question, but her class and jockey ensure she will set or contest the pace throughout.

runners_data.name: Liss Eile
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type with a prominent tendency to fade late (flagged); placed in midfield on the map only because the field has more backmarkers than the shape can absorb — her real position will likely be towards the rear, from where her OR of 77 and a form string of P-4-0-0-0 make improvement very hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Miss Fourie
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained mare returning from a 323-day absence, which is a serious fitness concern for a beginners' chase over this trip; she has two wins from 15 good-ground starts but both came some time ago, and her hold-up style means she relies on a pace collapse that this field is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Straight Home
runners_data.note: Lightly raced nine-year-old with an excellent record — three wins from 14 good-ground starts including two wins at 22f — but returns from a 426-day lay-off, which is the single biggest risk factor; headgear (t) and Brian Hayes in the saddle suggest Mullins is taking this seriously, and she profiles as a natural prominent racer who fits the likely shape well if fit enough.

races.paceDynamic: Future Prospect and La Note Verte are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over 2m6f on good ground at Tramore, creating an honest, competitive gallop throughout rather than a falsely run affair. With both trained by Willie Mullins and ridden by Danny Mullins and J J Slevin respectively, neither jockey is likely to cede the front willingly, meaning the pace will be genuine and sustained from flag to finish. Carry On Heidi, Costanuci, and Straight Home will press prominently behind that duel, compressing the field and leaving little room for hold-up horses to find gaps late. This race shape — a contested lead driving an honest gallop — strongly favours prominent racers who can track close to the friction and outstay it, rather than hold-up types who will struggle to deliver a meaningful late challenge on a track that does not generate significant finishes for closers. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Liss Eile is a genuine hold-up horse displaced to midfield on the map, but is unlikely to secure any meaningful tactical position, and Miss Fourie and Ellens Pride face the same structural problem of needing ground that this pace shape will not create.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Future Prospect and La Note Verte fight out the front from the start and the pace stays honest throughout the 2m6f trip.
scenarios.body: A genuine lead battle between two Mullins front-runners ensures the gallop never relents, burning off hold-up types and suiting the horse that tracks closest without over-committing early; the winner emerges from the prominent chasing group with enough left to collar whoever survives the lead duel.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leads, Tracks Win
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners gains a decisive advantage early and the other settles just off, with a close-tracking prominent horse timing a run to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A solo leader at a controlled but genuine gallop over this distance rewards a prominent horse who avoids the early friction and arrives fresh at the final obstacles; Straight Home's strong record on good ground and Carry On Heidi's consistency make them dangers here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the lead duel between Future Prospect and La Note Verte burns both horses out approaching the home straight and leaves a gap for a staying hold-up type.
scenarios.body: Even in this scenario, genuine hold-up horses like Miss Fourie face the disadvantage of a very long lay-off and Ellens Pride has shown no pattern of late-race surges on good ground; the beneficiary is more likely to be a midfield tracker than a true backmarker.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, falls, or tactical mistakes disrupt the field wholesale and the race loses its shape entirely with fences taking a toll on this beginners' chase field.
scenarios.body: A beginners' steeplechase with nine mares over 2m6f carries inherent jumping risk; Kaylasjet's poor recent form and Liss Eile's fading tendency make them vulnerable, but Carry On Heidi's sound jumping history and Straight Home's experience could exploit disarray.

watchPoints.text: Future Prospect and La Note Verte are both confirmed front-runners with top jockeys — watch the first fence for any sign of one yielding, as whoever gains the early rail position may control the race from there.

Straight Home returns after 426 days off and Liss Eile after 24 days with consistently poor form — both represent ends of the fitness spectrum and could be significant non-runners in terms of race impact if they fade or cause jumping interference.

Miss Fourie's 323-day absence for Gordon Elliott is worth tracking in the pre-race market; a significant move in price either way would be informative given Elliott's 4/42 last-14-day strike rate suggesting he is not in peak form.

This is a beginners' steeplechase — watch the quality of jumping at the early fences, particularly from Kaylasjet and Ellens Pride, whose form patterns suggest they may struggle with the technical demands of a chase over 2m6f on good ground.

Costanuci has raced 15 times on good ground without a win; if she drifts in the market pre-race despite John Queally's recent placed form, that is a signal to discount her further in scenarios that require genuine pace-pressing ability.

races.name: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John C McConnell returning quickly (8 days) in fine yard form (T14: 2/28); Good ground poses no concern and 20f+ trip history is solid, though a string of below-par efforts (U50-06) demands a bounceback performance at this trip.

runners_data.name: Marv Michael
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter here and central to the entire race shape; Harry Sexton (7lb claim) reduces the burden but the 62-day absence and a sequence of poor finishes (500-96) temper confidence, and his OR note flags the possibility he races out of character if pressed or if his jumping deserts him.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for the Cody yard who operates best when given a true pace to aim at; 14 days since last run is fine, Good ground and 20f+ trips are within his comfort zone, and his 2/20f run shows he can finish powerfully when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Nastya
runners_data.note: Strong prominent profile for De Bromhead (T14: 6/37, yard in excellent form) with two recent wins at 24f on Good ground suggesting trip and surface are ideal; the F in recent form is the one flag for jumping integrity, but when right she is clearly talented.

runners_data.name: Tullyveery Lad
runners_data.note: Last ran just two days ago which is a highly unusual and eyecatching preparation — whether that points to a significant target or a scheduling quirk must be weighed carefully; he is a prominent type with 2m6f form on Good ground, but the -502U5 recent record is poor and the blinkers are already fitted.

runners_data.name: Orkneys Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer stepping up from softer ground into Good, which is a positive surface switch given his best run (3/20f) came on Good; the 5lb claim for Alan O'Sullivan keeps the weight down to 152lbs, though he is without a win and his hold-up style requires a searching gallop to be seen to best effect.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse (10yo) whose recent form (6-4P90) is deeply unconvincing; no trainer recent form and a history dominated by Good ground haven't translated into results, and at OR 105 he is likely to need things to go wrong for others to get involved.

runners_data.name: A Snow White Park
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the mount for Margaret Mullins, which is a significant booking for a 5yo showing a promising placed profile (2-2-4 recently); naturally a hold-up racer by style, he has been pushed into the midfield on the pace map given the crowded rear of the field, which may mean he ends up racing further forward than ideal.

runners_data.name: That's About Right
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form with a hold-up style that suits staying races when pace is genuine; the tp headgear is already in place, and while his Good-ground record is fair (13/15 sim-going hits), he has been mapped into midfield rather than his preferred rear position, subtly compromising what he does best.

runners_data.name: Pourquoi Poi
runners_data.note: A 5yo with a staying profile and genuine prominent tendencies, but Daniel King's mount has been pushed back into the midfield map because of the crowded prominent group ahead; his trainer P W Flynn has had no recent winners (T14: 0/21), and a B (brought down) mars the recent form string — this is a difficult race to win for him.

races.paceDynamic: Marv Michael is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push the pace, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m6f trip on Good ground at Tramore. Intense Approach, Nastya, and Tullyveery Lad are all prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace, meaning there will be a tight cluster near the head of affairs from early on, but Marv Michael should not face a burning pressure duel. The field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Pourquoi Poi, A Snow White Park, and That's About Right are genuine prominent or hold-up types who have been pushed into the midfield map because they are unlikely to secure their natural position given the traffic ahead of them. With one unhurried leader setting a measured pace over a staying trip, the race shape is likeliest to favour prominent racers who travel smoothly just off the lead and can pick up once jumping the final two fences, rather than closers who will be forced into a more forward position than suits them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Marv Michael Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Marv Michael bowls along unchallenged and the pace remains honest but not brutal, setting up a test of jumping and stamina.
scenarios.body: Nastya and Intense Approach, tracking in the prominent group just off Marv Michael, are best positioned to pounce from the second-last fence as the leader's advantage is reeled in; both have strong Good-ground profiles and the race falls into their lap without a pace collapse or a sprint finish. Tullyveery Lad's course distance form also makes him dangerous in this shape, though recent form concerns temper expectations.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays All Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Marv Michael is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged and jumps cleanly, converting the race into a test of jumping accuracy over staying stamina.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to pressurise from an early stage, Marv Michael could build a lead that proves unassailable over this stiff 2m6f track; the layoff of 62 days is a slight concern but the style fit is near-perfect for this race shape despite the OR note. Hold-up horses and midfield types will find it hard to close a gap if the leader has stolen an advantage jumping the penultimate fence in good rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If a strong gallop develops through an unexpected pace injection from the prominent cluster and the field strings out, leaving ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Watch The Weather and Orkneys Jack, natural hold-up performers who can finish powerfully when the fractions are genuinely searching, would be the beneficiaries; both have Good-ground records and the longer trip plays to their staying strength. However, this scenario depends partly on horses like A Snow White Park and That's About Right actually racing from the rear as their true style demands, and their redistribution into midfield reduces confidence in a true late-closers shape materialising.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Falls, and Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the field suffers jumping errors, falls, or unseats that dramatically alter the race shape and thin the field.
scenarios.body: Tramore's fences can catch horses out, and with a ten-runner field and several horses showing U or F in recent form strings, attrition is a genuine possibility; Nastya (F in recent form) and Tullyveery Lad (U in recent form) are flagged as horses to watch in this respect. Whoever survives with a clear round and good position inherits the race — the prominent types closest to the pace hold the edge in survival scenarios.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tullyveery Lad's two-day turnaround closely — a horse racing again 48 hours after its last run is highly unusual and may signal either a deliberate plan or a yard error; if unconvincing early, his jumping may be compromised.

Nastya has an F (fall) in recent form and will be jumping fences on a jumping track — if her jumping is not fluent from the outset, Darragh O'Keeffe will face a difficult decision managing her prominent position.

If Marv Michael gets a flawless round of jumping and no horse applies early pressure, he could steal a lead that proves unmanageable — monitor whether any prominent rival tracks him aggressively from fence one or allows him to coast.

A Snow White Park and That's About Right will likely end up racing closer to the pace than their natural style demands; if either fights for position early rather than settling, it could waste energy that they need for the finish on this stiff 2m6f course.

General Clermont's market move (or lack of it) is worth noting — at OR 105 with poor recent form and a passive yard, any unexpected support would suggest local intelligence about a potential improvement.

races.name: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: Has placed three times on similar going over comparable trips and brings course familiarity as a 10-year-old, but his natural hold-up style means he is racing in a crowded back group and must find room; blinkers fitted, 47 days fresh.|

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Placed second at 17f on Good going just 44 days ago, which is his most relevant recent piece of form; Sean Flanagan is a key booking for a handler whose 14-day strike rate is quiet, and though this horse naturally prefers the rear, he is one of the more credible closers given his placed form at this distance and trip.|

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, and the axis around which this entire race pivots — sets a solo lead on Good ground at a track he knows, and his ability to control his own fractions without pressure is the dominant tactical fact of this race; OR 92, top-rated, handles this going.|

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Trainer Adrian Sexton has form with this mare, who is only 13 days between runs and wears headgear (hg:h); her genuine running style is as a hold-up horse occupying more ground than the map suggests, and her recent form figures of 774960 offer limited encouragement for making ground from a compressed closing group.|

runners_data.name: Kingdom Calling
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Eoin McCarthy whose trainer has a 1/9 14-day record — the one positive — but finishing position has faded in recent efforts and his historical tendency to drop away in the finish is a clear concern; this horse's natural home is at the rear, but with several rivals in the same zone he is squeezed for tactical room.|

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: Bernard Crowley's six-year-old has a strong preference for Good ground (14/15 runs on similar) and has placed twice in recent form; as the only genuine prominent-style runner behind the leader, she is ideally positioned to track Itsalonglongroad and challenge at the second-last without needing things to go her way.|

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: Four-year-old running only two days after his last start, which is a concern for freshness; Jordan Canavan takes the 7lb claim but this horse's Good-going record is thin (5/15 runs) and his form figures of 0P-P96 offer no encouragement for a competitive handicap chase at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Nobody
runners_data.note: Brendan Walsh's five-year-old showed a best finish of 5th at 17f on Good going, but his recent figures include two point-to-point blanks and he carries a fade-in-finish flag; as a natural hold-up horse in an already crowded closing group, he faces a difficult passage to land a blow.|

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins is a strong jockey booking for R Donohoe's five-year-old, who is only nine days since his last run; his historical form was achieved over much longer distances (20-24f), making this 1m7½f trip a notable drop in journey and a question mark hangs over whether he gets home at this pace.|

runners_data.name: Robin Elite
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old for Eugene O'Sullivan who is also only two days between runs and carries a fade-in-finish flag alongside blinkers and a tongue-tie; his historical record at 22-24f trips on Good going makes him an awkward fit for this shorter, sharper contest, and from a hold-up berth in a congested field, his chances look slim.|

races.paceDynamic: Itsalonglongroad is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap chase over 1m7½f at Tramore, and on Good ground is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo with no genuine rival to press him through the early stages. Polly Poppins is the only prominent-style runner who may track closely, but even she is unlikely to apply pressure enough to force Itsalonglongroad into a genuine battle. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Katherine, Kingdom Calling, Nobody, Ballinaboola Gold, and Robin Elite are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers to fit at the rear; in reality, the back half of this field will be congested with horses hunting cover, making it hard for any of them to find a clean, unimpeded run to the front. A lone front-runner setting an unhurried pace on Good ground over a sharp 1m7½f trip strongly favours the lead-and-prominent profile — horses who can travel within striking distance of Itsalonglongroad without burning fuel will have the decisive first run at the second-last, while the genuine closers face a muddled, traffic-heavy route home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Itsalonglongroad Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Itsalonglongroad bowls along at a comfortable gallop and has enough left in the tank to repel challengers from the second-last fence home.
scenarios.body: A 12-year-old with course experience, he sets a relaxed pace on Good going over a trip he handles, meaning rivals always have to come and find him rather than the reverse; at OR 92 he is top-rated and gets a clear run throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Polly Poppins or Bossing It tracks the pace efficiently and produces a sharp jump at the second-last to collar the leader before the final fence.
scenarios.body: This scenario suits a horse who can travel sweetly just off Itsalonglongroad without being drawn into a duel, then produce a decisive, well-timed challenge from a handy position; Good ground at Tramore with a short run-in rewards those with early position and a clean jump.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to drain Itsalonglongroad early and one of the redistributed closers finds a clear passage up the inner or outer in the straight.
scenarios.body: The congested nature of the hold-up group means this scenario depends on fortune as much as ability — one runner getting a gap while others are blocked, and delivering a late rattle to catch a tiring leader; Bossing It, who has placed twice at this distance on Good going, or Presenting Lad with similar-going form, are best-placed among the closers to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Itsalonglongroad is headed or blunders badly at a fence and the race breaks open into a scramble from two out.
scenarios.body: Without the front-runner dictating, the field becomes disorganised and a lower-weighted, fresh horse could capitalise on the chaos; Ballinaboola Gold, carrying the minimum weight and fresh off a nine-day turnaround, or Ray Gun as a young improving type, are marginal beneficiaries of a messy end.

watchPoints.text: Polly Poppins is the one runner who can organically slot in just behind Itsalonglongroad and produce a clean, unimpeded challenge — if she travels sweetly to two out she is the most dangerous threat to the leader.

The cluster of five redistributed hold-up types (Katherine, Kingdom Calling, Nobody, Ballinaboola Gold, Robin Elite) will be jostling for position in the same part of the field — watch for traffic trouble and interference between the last two fences that could compromise several runners simultaneously.
Ray Gun and Robin Elite both ran within the last two days — monitor market moves and any late scratchings as fitness and recovery from such quick returns are legitimate concerns in a handicap chase.

Itsalonglongroad's jumping should be watched from the outset — as a 12-year-old front-runner, any error at an early fence could dramatically reshape the race and hand the initiative to Polly Poppins or Bossing It tracking just behind.

Bossing It's jockey Sean Flanagan is likely to make an early decision about whether to hunt Itsalonglongroad or drop in — where he positions the horse in the first half-mile will define whether he arrives with a meaningful challenge or gets swallowed up in the hold-up group.
